title: P7 · Back home
description: Kamal comes home. His GP in Kuala Terengganu does not know he was treated in Mina. After the story this guide tells.
where: A GP clinic in Kuala Terengganu

cast.description: Malaysian man, 61, slim, short grey hair, kind face. Batik shirt in Malaysia. In KSA, white two-piece ihram (unstitched towelling cloth, right shoulder bare when in ihram), a small waist pouch and one phone.
His wife, about 58. White modest Hajj outfit and white telekung-style hijab in KSA; pastel baju kurung and tudung in Malaysia.
Malaysian GP, late 30s, tudung, white coat.

notes: Ihram (two white unstitched sheets) is for men only; women wear ordinary modest clothing, usually white, face and hands uncovered.

steps.title: Back home
steps.headline: Kamal is home and well, but his GP does not know he was treated in Mina.
steps.where: A GP clinic in Kuala Terengganu
steps.narrative: Kamal comes home. His GP in Kuala Terengganu does not know he was treated in Mina. After the story this guide tells.

experiences.doing: Sees Kamal back home, with nothing in her record of his care in KSA.
experiences.feeling: “Treated in Mina? Nothing came back to me.”

experiences.doing: Tells her, as best he remembers, what happened.
experiences.feeling: “They gave me a drip… I don't remember what else.”

experiences.doing: Fills in what he does not remember.
experiences.feeling: “Someone should have sent it to her.”

steps.painPoint: The record of care abroad, and who opened his summary, never comes home.
steps.enabler: Nothing yet: the guide does not specify a return path.
steps.policy: Should the host country send a summary of care back to the home country — and with whose consent?
gaps: Nothing returns the record of care in KSA, or a log of who opened his summary, to Malaysia.

illustration.alt: Back in Kuala Terengganu, Kamal in a white kopiah and Salmah sit with Dr Aisyah, who looks at her computer with a question mark: the record of his care in Saudi Arabia has not come home.
illustration.prompt: Kuala Terengganu: Kamal, healthy, in batik with a white kopiah, sits with Dr Aisyah in her clinic, Salmah beside him. Dr Aisyah looks at her computer with a gentle question-mark bubble: she doesn't know what happened in KSA. To the side, a faint dotted arc from a small Saudi building icon toward the clinic fades out halfway with a gap. Warm but slightly unresolved.

record.description: Home again; his GP does not yet know he was treated
